subject: QBR kickoff: goal commitments, owner decisions, and QBR packet responsibilities
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR kickoff: goal commitments, owner decisions, and QBR packet responsibilities

Team —

We're kicking off the quarter and I want to lock owners and sign-offs for the OKRs we'll present at the QBR. This is a focused request — please review the attached Q2_goals_draft_v3.xlsx and the one-page QBR_packet_outline.docx. High-level asks: 

1) Owners: confirm who will be the primary and secondary owner on each objective by EOD tomorrow (Friday).
2) Metrics: confirm the single metric we'll report for each key result (no more than one metric per KR in the packet).
3) Runbooks & risks: note any rollout/risk items you want surfaced in the QBR notes tab.

Initial proposed owners are in column D in the workbook. For the AtlasHealth integration (external ops copied), I flagged the rollout window as "late May" — Vivek, can you confirm whether that still holds with the SRE/infra plan?

I'll consolidate decisions into a short decision_log_20270415.md and a finalized packet on Monday morning.

Attachments: Q2_goals_draft_v3.xlsx (workbook), QBR_packet_outline.docx (1-pager)

Thanks — short replies welcome, we just need clear ownership.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Product Ops | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR kickoff: goal commitments, owner decisions, and QBR packet responsibilities

Thanks Neha — I reviewed the workbook and LGTM overall. Quick notes: 

- I'll take primary ownership of Objective 1 (Runtime Stability) and assign Priya (CS Eng) as secondary — I'll add her to the doc later today.
- For KR1.2 (p95 latency), let's use the 7-day rolling p95 as the single metric. We need the chart for the packet.
- Suggestion: add a one-line context bullet under each objective in the packet outline that ties the customer impact to the metric (helps the exec read).

I approve the packet outline subject to the one-line context bullets.

Laura Bennett
VP, Engineering | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Neha / Laura —

I'll own Objective 2 (Cost Efficiency & Serving Economics) as primary. A couple of clarifying asks: 

- For KR2.1 we currently have a blended tokens-per-second cost target. Can we break out the target into hosted API vs dedicated instances? The finance team will want to see both.
- I can produce a short slide with current baseline numbers and projected delta; need final owner confirmations by Monday COB so I can finish the numbers.

Sara (Procurement) — can you confirm if the AtlasHealth PO timeline (attached in the procurement thread) still expects a May invoice? If so we should call out billing timing in the QBR notes.

-marcuS
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Economics | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR kickoff: goal commitments, owner decisions, and QBR packet responsibilities

Confirmed — late May rollout window still stands from infra side but two caveats: 

1) We need a preflight KV-cache sizing test (will require a short spike test) — SRE estimates 3 business days to run and analyze.
2) If AtlasHealth requires field-level encryption (they've asked in prior comms), that adds ~2 weeks of dev work and will shift the window. Marcus, happy to sync on the cost delta if that becomes a hard constraint.

I'll create a short runbook stub in the decision log with the testing timeline and owners by EOD Monday.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

- Please include a short line under "Risks" about contractual milestones tied to billing (helps legal/procurement).
- If you're calling out a latency target for AtlasHealth traffic, note the expected percent of traffic that will route to dedicated versus hosted (we'll need it for our capacity planning).
